reasoning: All three models reached 'inconclusive' due to a 413 Request Entity Too Large error when attempting to audit src/package/augment.mjs. However, this is a tool error, not a security finding. The file in question is upstream application code (the main entry point of the @augmentcode/auggie npm package), not AUR packaging code. Per the threat model, we audit for code INJECTED into AUR packaging (PKGBUILD, .install hooks, patches, wrapper scripts). The PKGBUILD is clean: sources are pinned with b2sums from official npm registry, uses hardened npm flags (--offline --ignore-scripts --no-audit), and the auggie.js wrapper is a legitimate AUR pattern that blocks self-updates. No malicious injection exists in the AUR packaging layer. The tool error on upstream code should not block a safe verdict for the packaging.
coverage_issues: All three models failed to audit src/package/augment.mjs due to 413 Request Entity Too Large error - this is a tool infrastructure issue, not a security gap
Models incorrectly treated a tool error on upstream application code as grounds for 'inconclusive' verdict, when the threat model only requires auditing AUR packaging files
false_positives: All three models' 'inconclusive' verdict is a false positive - the 413 error on augment.mjs (upstream code) should not block a safe verdict for AUR packaging, which was fully reviewed and found clean
learnings: Tool errors (413, timeouts, crashes) on files should be recorded as coverage_issues but should NOT automatically force an 'inconclusive' verdict - the verdict should reflect whether the AUR packaging layer (the actual threat model target) was successfully audited

Models need clearer guidance that upstream application code (files inside src/package/ that are part of the npm tarball) is out of scope for AUR injection audits - only PKGBUILD, .install hooks, local wrapper scripts, and patches are in scope
When all reviewed AUR packaging files are safe and the only unaudited file is upstream application code, the correct verdict is 'safe' with a note about the coverage gap, not 'inconclusive'
